title: Scope
summary: Where a name is visible and alive. Locals live from their declaration to the end of their block; inner blocks see outer locals, but never the other way around.

details.heading: What is a block
details.body: A chunk is the body of a function, `if`/`elseif`/`else` branch, `for`/`while`/`repeat` loop, or an explicit `do ... end`. Each `end`/`until` closes a scope.

details.heading: Lookup rule
details.body: When Luau sees a name, it searches from the innermost block outward. The first matching local wins. If none is found, the name is treated as a global (`_G` lookup).

details.heading: Shadowing
details.body: Declaring a local with the same name as an outer local hides the outer one inside the new block. Legal, but a frequent source of bugs.

explanation.whatItIs: Scope is the 'territory' where a variable exists. Declare a local inside a function, and the rest of the script cannot see it. Understanding scope answers 'why is this nil here?'.
explanation.whyItExists: Scope keeps names from colliding, lets you reuse names like `i` in ten different loops, and makes code localizable: to understand a block you only look at that block.
whenToUse: Declare variables in the *narrowest* scope that works — inside the loop if only the loop uses them
Read outward when confused: where was this name declared?
whenNotToUse: Don't declare everything at script top 'to be safe' — it widens lifetimes and hides intent
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
local a = 1          -- script scope
if true then
    local b = 2      -- if-block scope
    print(a, b)      --> 1 2   (inner sees outer)
end
print(a)             --> 1
print(b)             --> nil   (outer can't see inner)
```
Scopes nest like boxes. A variable lives in the box it was declared in — visible inside, invisible outside.
tips: If a value is nil 'for no reason', 90% of the time it's a scope issue — the variable was declared in a block that already ended
Loop variables (`for i = ...`) exist only inside the loop
Functions close over the locals they can see — see closures
commonMistakes: Declaring inside an `if`, expecting to use it after the `end`
Shadowing: `local coins = coins + 1` reads the *new* (nil) local, not the outer one
Naming a local `script`, `wait`, or another builtin and wondering why the builtin stopped working

examples.title: Seeing scope boundaries
examples.code:
local count = 0

for i = 1, 3 do
    local doubled = i * 2      -- fresh each iteration
    count = count + doubled
end

print(count)      --> 12
print(doubled)    --> nil  — its scope ended with the loop
print(i)          --> nil  — loop variable is gone too

examples.title: The shadowing trap
examples.code:
local coins = 10

do
    local coins = coins + 5   -- BUG: new local, reads itself (nil)
    print(coins)              --> nil + 5 = error!
end
examples.commonMistake: Within its own initializer, the new `coins` is already in scope but unassigned. Don't redeclare with the same name.
